facts.text: Alarm fatigue is the state in which a person stops reacting to alarms, including important alarms, after hearing too many alarms that did not matter.
facts.quote: Alarm fatigue is the state in which a person has heard so many alarms that did not matter that they stop reacting to alarms at all, including the one that does matter.

facts.text: ISO 21815-3 notes that false positives could create alarm fatigue.
facts.quote: ISO 21815-3 notes that false positives "could create alarm fatigue" [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The booklet found no direct measurements of alarm fatigue in mining, such as the probability of ignoring the nth warning.
facts.quote: The booklet looked for direct measurements in mining, such as the probability of ignoring the nth warning, and found none [Chapter 4].

facts.text: The booklet found precursors and outcomes of alarm fatigue in mining: very high exposure to unnecessary alarms, annoyance, degraded trust, disabling and overriding.
facts.quote: It found the precursors and the outcomes: very high exposure to unnecessary alarms, annoyance, degraded trust, disabling and overriding [Chapter 4].

facts.text: NIOSH warned that operators may lose confidence in the warning system and start ignoring alarms altogether.
facts.quote: NIOSH warned that operators may "lose confidence in the system and start to ignore alarms altogether" [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Some truck warning data showed a strong cry-wolf effect, in which exposure to unnecessary warnings leads to ignoring warnings.
facts.quote: Road and aviation evidence is mixed: a cry-wolf effect was strong in some truck warning data

facts.text: Air-traffic-control alerts showed no cry-wolf effect despite having 45% false alarms.
facts.quote: absent in air-traffic-control alerts with 45% false alarms

facts.text: Some driving-simulator studies found no cry-wolf effect from warnings.
Operators of the existing warning fleet may already have learned to ignore frequent warnings and may bring that habit to their first automatic stops.
facts.quote: Operators of the existing warning fleet may already have learned to ignore frequent warnings, and will meet the first automatic stops with that habit [Chapter 1].

facts.text: A warning stage in the intervention ladder only buys time if operators still believe the warning.
facts.quote: A warning stage in the intervention ladder only buys time if the warning is still believed.
